referenceContract.note: REFERENCE_PARITY_MODE is preserved unchanged; this contract neither replaces nor edits it.

admissibilityRules.simulatorException: A ONE-STEP simulation on an isolated copy is admissible only inside DEPLOYABLE_WITH_SIMULATOR, and only when the deploying environment declares SIMULATOR_ONE_STEP as a supported runtime capability. It is an environment capability that must be declared, never a universal Sentinel assumption.
admissibilityRules.hiddenStateNote: The Forge kernel exposes complete world state internally. Internal availability is not deployable admissibility: deployable features read the decision-time observation packet, the legal action surface, and decision-time expert evidence derived from those — never authoritative world state the observer was not given.

missingValueSemantics.rule: A feature whose required capability or evidence is absent reports status UNAVAILABLE (capability not declared) or UNKNOWN (capability declared but evidence insufficient) with value=null. It is never defaulted to 0, false, or a neutral value, and the profile reports itself unsatisfied rather than emitting a dense vector.

findings.claim: The frozen Stage 3E extractor header admits branch rewardVector components as "runtime-visible one-step" evidence, but training records bind rewardVector to the branch TOTAL reward vector — the greedy-continuation horizon rollout total (src/forge/record-v2.js). Seven features were admitted under a one-step justification while carrying multi-step rollout totals.
findings.consequence: Those seven features are REQUIRES_MULTI_STEP_ROLLOUT here and are excluded from every deployable profile.

findings.claim: The Stage 3F.5 runtime adapter computed `energy` from the authoritative world constraint record — privileged state the observer was never given — rather than from the observation packet. Stage 3F.6 measured REMOVE_RESOURCE_SIGNALS changing 0 of 51 features, because degrading the observation cannot move a feature that never read it.
findings.consequence: resources.actorEnergy is bound to the observation vector, so resource degradation becomes observable.

findings.claim: Entity and relation counts appear twice in the observation packet: numeric vector positions 7 and 8, and the length of metadata.canonicalState.entities / .relationships. The Stage 3F.6 degradation harness edits the structured form only, so the two encodings can disagree under degradation.
findings.consequence: context.entityCount and context.relationCount bind to canonicalState, the same evidence the relational expert reads, so a degraded observation degrades them consistently.

findings.claim: No feature in this contract consumes actor position, so HIDE_SPATIAL_INFORMATION changes nothing here. This matches the Stage 3F.6 measurement of 0 features changed, and is a limitation inherited from the Stage 3E feature set, not a defect repaired by this contract.
findings.consequence: Recorded as a known blind spot rather than presented as a fix.

findings.claim: The environment one-step transition reward vector never declares futureObjectivePotential, optionValue, or terminalOutcome. Across 6723 one-step transitions covering all 28 scenario families at levels 1-3 over 6 seeds, with 0 generation failures, each of the three was declared 0 times; they appear only on the oracle branch TOTAL reward vector, which is a horizon rollout total. Because the Stage 3F.5 runtime adapter read them with a `?? 0` default, the runtime features greedyFuturePotential, greedyOptionValue and greedyTerminalOutcome were constant zero rather than measured quantities.
findings.consequence: The three corresponding one-step features report UNKNOWN whenever the environment does not declare the component, so an undeclared quantity can never again masquerade as a measured zero.

findings.claim: Stage 3F.6 certified oneStepConsequenceReadsObservation=false: the one-step consequence path read privileged state rather than the observation.
findings.consequence: Every DEPLOYABLE_WITH_SIMULATOR feature is derived from an injected one-step capability over an isolated copy, and the context and relational features that gate it read the observation.

spatial.note: Actor position is present in the observation (vector 3,4) and spatialState is a World State section, but no inherited Stage 3E feature consumes position. This contract stays spatially blind rather than inventing a feature.

risk.note: risk is a Stage 3F prediction domain with no corresponding World State section. Threat structure reaches deployable features through observed relational signals (threatened / unsupported / uncovered counts), not a risk fact.

constraints.note: The energy budget is observed directly at vector position 2 and is consumed by resources.actorEnergy.

worldStateCoverageAudit.calibrationStatusClaims: NONE. The Stage 3F.2 artifact records no resolved per-domain calibration status, so no feature in this contract is conditioned on a calibration-status claim.

v2bAvailability.evidence: The V2B adapter is archive-only (Stage 3F.6-R); no runtime expert produces genuine V2B answers.
v2bAvailability.substitutionNote: Another candidate producer must never be presented as V2B. Without the genuine expert the five V2B features report UNAVAILABLE and the DEPLOYABLE_WITH_V2B profile reports itself unsatisfied.

routerCompatibility.reason: The frozen Stage 3E router consumes 51 standardized features in a fixed key order, 21 of which are not admissible here (7 rollout-derived, 5 V2B-dependent, 9 simulator-dependent). DEPLOYABLE_CORE supplies 30 and DEPLOYABLE_WITH_SIMULATOR supplies 46 under redefined identities, so the frozen weight vector cannot be applied.
routerCompatibility.nextStepRequiresAuthorization: Retraining or refitting any router on this contract is out of scope for Stage 3F.6-S.

roadmap.nextRecommendedAction: Decide whether to authorize fitting a router on DEPLOYABLE_CORE or DEPLOYABLE_WITH_SIMULATOR, then authorize fresh topology-disjoint, disjoint-seed HOLDOUT/OOD generation for a confirmatory Stage 3F.6.
